summary: This is a Snowflake documentation reference page for the SNOWFLAKE.ALERT.LAST_SUCCESSFUL_SCHEDULED_TIME() function. It returns the scheduled time of the most recent successful alert condition evaluation, where no errors occurred and the alert state was CONDITION_FALSE or TRIGGERED. The function takes no arguments, returns a TIMESTAMP_LTZ value (or NULL if there are no recent successful evaluations), and is defined in the ALERT schema of the SNOWFLAKE database. Calling it requires a role granted the snowflake.alert_viewer database role.
one_line: Reference for the Snowflake function that returns the scheduled time of the most recent successful alert evaluation.
key_facts: SNOWFLAKE.ALERT.LAST_SUCCESSFUL_SCHEDULED_TIME() returns the timestamp representing the scheduled time for the most recent successful evaluation of the alert condition.
A successful evaluation for this function is one where no errors occurred and the alert history state is CONDITION_FALSE or TRIGGERED.
The function takes no arguments; its syntax is SNOWFLAKE.ALERT.LAST_SUCCESSFUL_SCHEDULED_TIME().
The function returns a TIMESTAMP_LTZ value.
The function returns NULL if there are no recent successful evaluations of the alert condition.
The function is defined in the ALERT schema of the SNOWFLAKE database.
To call the function, the user must use a role that is granted the snowflake.alert_viewer database role.
The example grant statement is: GRANT DATABASE ROLE snowflake.alert_viewer TO ROLE alert_role;
The note's example describes granting the snowflake.alert_viewer database role to a role named alert_role so it can call the function.
The page's usage notes section describes the function's schema location and required privilege.
